title: The Institutionalization of Responsible Management Education
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School, University of Hamburg and Trinity College Dublin

detail.title: The Institutionalization of Responsible Management Education

publicationDetails.detailsText:
In book: THE SAGE HANDBOOK OF RESPONSIBLE MANAGEMENT LEARNING AND EDUCATION
Publisher: SAGE

detail.abstract: This chapter discusses the institutionalization of responsible management education (RME). We start by reviewing different types of institutional pressures that have shaped the diffusion of RME, and we also discuss the relevance of selected institutional entrepreneurs which have influenced the acceptance of RME as a legitimized social practice. The following section focuses on the current status of institutionalization by demonstrating that many schools only symbolically adopt RME and hence decouple their public commitments from actual implementation practices. We review different types of decoupling in the business school context and discuss what determines whether a school decouples or not. The final section takes a look into the future and outlines an agenda for forthcoming scholarly work in this area. This section also discusses in what ways educational and organizational practices can be improved to avoid decoupling and to therefore move more strongly towards substantive implementation of RME.

title: The Real Effects of Bankruptcy Reform
affiliations: Peking University - HSBC School of Business and Peking University HSBC Business School

detail.title: The Real Effects of Bankruptcy Reform
detail.abstract: We construct the most comprehensive bankruptcy database of Chinese firms to date and document significant real effects arising from the establishment of specialized bankruptcy courts. Specifically, the recovery rate for unsecured creditors increases by 38.6 percentage points after the reform. This improvement is not driven by shorter case durations or lower direct bankruptcy costs, as intuition might suggest. Instead, it results primarily from greater efficiency in the discovery and disposal of assets during bankruptcy proceedings. The reform also increases the likelihood of reorganization and promotes capital infusion in such cases. Higher recovery rates generate broader spillovers: reductions in non-performing loans, expansion of unsecured lending by local banks, relaxation of firms' financial constraints, shifts in capital structure and investment, and greater public willingness to file for bankruptcy when distressed.

title: UAV Food Delivery Route Planning Based on Improved Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Algorithm
affiliations: Shanghai Dianji University, Shanghai Dianji University, Shanghai Dianji University and Shanghai Dianji University

detail.title: UAV Food Delivery Route Planning Based on Improved Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Algorithm
detail.abstract: Drone-based food delivery is a key approach to addressing the bottleneck of the “last-mile” distribution problem. To enhance the timeliness, safety, and cost controllability of food delivery in high-density urban areas, this study investigates the optimization of drone delivery routes within a three-dimensional urban airspace. First, the immediacy and multi-node characteristics of food delivery are analyzed, and a three-dimensional airspace model is constructed using real geographic data from Shanghai. Second, constraints such as building occlusion and airspace conflicts are modeled, and penalty functions are introduced for issues such as delivery delays and excessive energy consumption. Third, considering dynamic orders, airspace regulations, and endurance limitations, a multi-objective optimization model is developed with delivery timeliness, energy consumption, and food safety as the objectives. Finally, an improved Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) algorithm is proposed, incorporating dynamic weight adjustment and spatial awareness mechanisms, to obtain feasible three-dimensional delivery routes for high-density urban environments. Simulation-based comparative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in scenarios such as commercial district peak periods and residential community delivery. This study provides theoretical and technical support for drone delivery route planning and platform scheduling.

title: Judicial Institution and Innovation: Evidence from China's Intellectual Property Courts Reform
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law,  and Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

detail.title: Judicial Institution and Innovation: Evidence from China's Intellectual Property Courts Reform

keywords: China's Intellectual Property Courts JEL Classification: K42

detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of intellectual property judicial institutions on innovation, focusing on the intellectual property courts (IPCs) reform in China. We find that IPCs reform leads to a significant 22.6% increase in the number of invention patents at the city level, equating to an average rise of 215 annually. Notably, we rule out the possibility of inter-region and intra-conglomerate transfer of patents, indicating that the effect of the IPCs reform on innovation is not a zero-sum game among regions. Furthermore, we find that the IPCs reform alters the patent structure by shifting the focus from utility and design patents to invention patents; however, it does not appear to significantly improve invention patent quality. Mechanism analyses suggest that the IPCs reform increases social satisfaction with judicial protection of intellectual property, shorter case duration and higher plaintiff winning rates in intellectual property cases.

title: The End of Game Theory: Designing Positive-Sum Systems for the Digital Commons
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The End of Game Theory: Designing Positive-Sum Systems for the Digital Commons
detail.abstract:
For decades, game theory has provided the dominant lens for understanding economic and social interaction. Rooted in assumptions of scarcity and strategic conflict, it frames individuals as actors locked in zero-sum games where one party’s gain is another’s loss (Nash, 1950). Even cooperative variants often rely on fragile governance arrangements, where self-interest must be constrained for the collective good. The tragedy of the commons (Hardin, 1968) has long been emblematic of these tensions, suggesting collapse is inevitable without rules, punishments, or external enforcement.

Elinor Ostrom’s Nobel-winning work demonstrated that communities could self-organize to preserve common resources (Ostrom, 1990). This was a profound correction to deterministic collapse models. Yet even Ostrom’s framework still presumes the underlying tension between self-interest and collective interest — that human behavior must be moderated, negotiated, or disciplined to prevent exhaustion of shared goods.

This paper advances a more radical proposition: what if we could design systems where self-interest itself expands the commons, rather than depleting it? What if the very conditions that once produced tragedy now guaranteed resilience? Such a framework would render the core assumptions of game theory obsolete, replacing adversarial logic with architectures that are inherently positive-sum.

title: The OZII Framework: Rethinking Global Industrial Governance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The OZII Framework: Rethinking Global Industrial Governance
detail.abstract: In response to the systemic shortcomings of traditional economic zones in a fragmented world, this paper introduces the OZII-Global Special Industrial Authority System, a new model of industrial governance designed to address modern challenges in supply chains, technological sovereignty, and inclusive growth. Unlike conventional economic zones, OZII is structured as a legally autonomous authority with global-standard oversight, AI-driven management, and long-term industrial transfer mechanisms. It serves as a living laboratory for testing governance models that reconcile economic dynamism with social justice and sustainability. OZII is the first institutional application of the broader OZINomy paradigm-a socioeconomic framework designed to respond to a world increasingly divided by geopolitical rivalries and fragmented governance. While OZII is the initial laboratory, OZINomy can guide other governance experiments globally.

title: The Legitimacy of Sustainability Standards: A Paradox Perspective
affiliations: Swiss Finance Institute - HEC Lausanne and Copenhagen Business School

detail.title: The Legitimacy of Sustainability Standards: A Paradox Perspective
detail.abstract: Sustainability standards have proliferated widely in recent years but their legitimacy remains contested. This paper suggests that sustainability standards need to cope with an important but unexplored paradox to gain legitimacy. While standard setters create low entry barriers and requirements for adopters so that standards can diffuse quickly and achieve a status of cognitive legitimacy, standards also need to ensure that adopters create high levels of impact, thereby acquiring moral legitimacy. While the need for diffusion and impact occurs at the same time, they cannot be achieved simultaneously. We unpack this paradox and show that its salience for standard setters differs depending on (a) the growth trajectory of a standard and (b) the perceived intensity of the demands for diffusion and impact. We outline five response strategies that standard setters can use to tackle the diffusion–impact paradox and illustrate our theoretical considerations through a detailed case study of the UN Global Compact. Our paper advances scholarly understandings on how sustainability standards gain legitimacy and sheds light on the complex and inherently paradoxical nature of legitimacy. We derive implications for the literatures on sustainability standards, legitimacy, and paradox management.

title: Recommended technology management of smart policing robocops for AI ethics and cybersecurity
affiliations: Kelley School of Business, Independent and National Louis University

detail.title: Recommended technology management of smart policing robocops for AI ethics and cybersecurity
detail.abstract: The videotaped murders of George Floyd and Tyre Nichols in the United States have raised awareness worldwide of police misconduct. Police and citizens now distrust and fear each other because of the prevalence of instances of police brutality. Numerous incidents of police brutality indicate that policing requires a radical redesign that takes human rights into account. There is a greater need for smart policing technology management research as a result of new, increasingly ubiquitous technologies. Robotics and surveillance cameras are examples of smart policing. In several jurisdictions worldwide, currently robocops are on patrol and some can be armed, e.g., the recent approval for use in San Francisco. Given its perceived inherit technical objectivity, well managed smart technology has the potential to improve policing and ethical outcomes. With adequate technology management, smart policing can potentially alleviate law enforcement racial bias and abuse. This critically appraised topic study finds that there are few studies that address this issue. The defund the police movement calls for the reallocation of funds toward community services and community policing. In 2021, there was also a call for the US Congress to approve the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act. This research revealed that there are few studies that tackle this problem. With this critically appraised topic literature review, we make seven (7) recommendations on how resources can be effectively spent toward efficient law enforcement that leads to long overdue police reform using smart policing robocops.

title: The Effects of K-12 Computer Science Education Policies on Postsecondary CS Participation
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - College of Education, University of Missouri, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Department of Computer Science

detail.title: The Effects of K-12 Computer Science Education Policies on Postsecondary CS Participation

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Science Foundation under grant numbers 2317943 and 2317944.

detail.abstract: States have increasingly adopted policies to promote computer science education at the elementary and secondary levels. These policies are intended, in part, to promote the pursuit of computer science at the postsecondary level. We collect novel longitudinal data on adoption and implementation dates of nine policies promoted by the Code.org Advocacy Coalition in the United States since 2000 and use event study methods to evaluate their impacts on computer science undergraduate degree completion and teacher certification. We find little evidence that any policy we consider has meaningful impacts on either outcome. We conclude that these policies are too light-touch to matter and largely reflect, rather than cause, rising interest in computer science among undergraduates.

title: Motivating Entrepreneur Educators: A Simulation-Based Approach to Faculty Evaluation and Role Alignment
affiliations: Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management, Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management and Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management

detail.title: Motivating Entrepreneur Educators: A Simulation-Based Approach to Faculty Evaluation and Role Alignment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: the authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human or animal subjects were involved. The study used simulations and narrative analysis; thus, ethical approval and consent were not required. This study used no human subjects, institutional data, or identifiable information. All simulations were based on theoretically constructed profiles and scores derived from published vocational and motivational models. No ethical approval was required. However, proposed evaluation reforms—if adopted—may alter institutional incentive structures and merit further ethical reflection at the policy level.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded,

detail.abstract: This study aims to develop and validate a policy-relevant faculty evaluation model that aligns institutional assessment practices with differentiated academic roles and motivational factors, particularly for entrepreneurship-oriented educators in Indonesian higher education. The problem addressed is the persistent reliance on the uniform Tri Dharma framework, which fails to recognize and reward diverse academic contributions outside traditional teaching, research, and service, leading to demotivation among entrepreneurial faculty and misalignment with national innovation policies. The study employs Monte Carlo simulations to compare three evaluative approaches: equal-weighted roles, the existing Tri Dharma criteria, and a proposed model incorporating motivational theories (Vroom, Herzberg, Ryan & Deci) and vocational fit (Holland’s RIASEC typology). Results indicate that the current system structurally penalizes faculty engaged in non-Tri Dharma roles, whereas the proposed framework maintains motivational alignment and enables role-based differentiation. This is significant because without reform, institutions risk undermining innovation goals through policy-practice misalignment; the model offers a scalable and evidence-based tool for aligning faculty assessment with strategic policy imperatives.

title: Watt's Next: Navigating the Surge in Electric Vehicle Adoption and its Implications for Grid Operations
affiliations: University College London - UCL School of Management, Oregon State University - College of Business, Indiana University - Kelley School of Business and University of Alabama

detail.title: Watt's Next: Navigating the Surge in Electric Vehicle Adoption and its Implications for Grid Operations
detail.abstract: The rapid electrification of transportation is a cornerstone of decarbonization efforts, yet it may also increase peak electricity demand and places substantial strain on existing grid infrastructure. At the same time, electric vehicles (EVs) offer the potential to mitigate these issues via managed charging and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technologies. This paper explores how an integrated energy system planner can optimally manage EVs and stationary battery storage to minimize system-wide costs and emissions. We develop a stylized analytical model that accounts for EV drivers' driving needs, the proportion of them willing to enroll in managed charging programs, and the degree of flexibility they are willing to offer. We derive optimal grid operations for a simplified setting with two periods (peak and off-peak) per day and show that the key insights extend to a higher-fidelity 24-hour model calibrated with real data from the PJM interconnection region. We find that the interplay between EVs and grid-scale batteries is non-trivial-they can be substitutes or complements in the system planner's portfolio. We also extend the model to incorporate EV drivers with heterogeneous default charging behaviors. By capturing the fundamental trade-offs involved in managing EVs and stationary storage, our model offers a useful foundation for designing effective grid management strategies and EV charging programs. Utilities and policymakers should prioritize expanding participation in managed charging programs, particularly among drivers with peak-time charging habits. Investments in stationary storage should be aligned with EV adoption and management trajectories to prevent inefficiencies. While high EV adoption is desirable, its benefits depend critically on user behavior and system integration strategies.

reference: Book title: Trust, Safety, and the Internet We Share: Multistakeholder Insights (2025)
title: Intersections Between Trust, Safety, and Responsible AI How Trust & Safety and AI Auditing Can Learn and Evolve Together

detail.title: Intersections Between Trust, Safety, and Responsible AI How Trust & Safety and AI Auditing Can Learn and Evolve Together

publicationDetails.detailsText: Book title: Trust, Safety, and the Internet We Share: Multistakeholder Insights (2025)

detail.abstract: AI Responsibility is a critical focus in today's tech landscape. Trust and Safety (T&S) teams have traditionally played a crucial role in risk assessment and mitigation, applying their expertise to ensure product experiences align with company values and enhance user trust. While T&S risk assessment often operates at a feature or content level, increasing adoption of AI suggests practitioners may benefit from lessons learned in assessing risks for AI/ML systems across the technical stack in order to address safety at scale. AI Responsibility and T&S have historically been somewhat distinct domains, with the former often embedded in research or engineering teams and the latter positioned differently across companies, but often in business related functions. However, there is a growing convergence between these areas. Integration points could significantly enhance responsibility practices by leveraging T&S functions which often apply across the entire business. This chapter introduces a new framework that enables practitioners to draw from insights across both domains to make AI products safer. Generative AI introduces new opportunities and challenges for T&S across traditional functions like content moderation, as well as novel safety issues such as jailbreaking or hallucinations. With new opportunities for abuse, as well as new capabilities, teams must develop enhanced safety tools and processes around AI systems, anticipating distinct issues in different stages of development. This chapter explores increasing intersection points between T&S and Responsible AI, describing tools to equip T&S teams and other interested stakeholders for this rapidly evolving landscape.

title: Endogenous Entry in Networked Markets with Production and Edge Capacity Constraints
affiliations: Clemson University, Stanford University and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Endogenous Entry in Networked Markets with Production and Edge Capacity Constraints
detail.abstract: Motivated by electricity markets, we investigate the key drivers of firm entry and investment in multiregional markets with elastic demand, incorporating capacity constraints for both firms and transportation. These constraints introduce externalities due to the coupling of decisions across firms and regions. To address such complication, we extend the conventional networked Cournot competition framework to consider endogenous entry on capacitated general networks, and develop a novel convex optimization model that is substantially more tractable than the commonly-used mixed complementarity problem formulations. This model enables us to prove the uniqueness of the equilibrium, analyze how factors such as entry locations and tariffs shape investment decisions, and carry out a case study on a realistic electricity market dataset. We find that a well-chosen firm entry location not only benefits the firm's own profit, but may also bring positive externalities for incumbent firms and consumers. Additionally, we show that import tariffs may, counterintuitively, encourage the expansion of more efficient foreign firms. Our results offer both novel analytical frameworks and scalable computational tools for practitioners, guiding efficient investment of capacity and infrastructure in networked markets.

title: Reverse Engineering Innovation
affiliations: Brigham Young University and Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr School of Business, Purdue University

detail.title: Reverse Engineering Innovation
detail.abstract: We examine whether reverse engineering activities undertaken by firms are influenced by the extent of trade secrecy in competitor firms. We develop a novel measure for reverse engineering based on abnormal purchasing patterns of peer firm products around firm headquarters, using the Nielsen scanner database. We validate this measure by showing that firms with greater abnormal purchasing behavior near their headquarters are more likely to introduce products and technologies that more closely resemble competitors’ offerings, and that competitors experience declines in gross margin when they are subject to higher levels of reverse engineering activity. Using this measure, we find that competitors’ use of trade secrecy is associated with increased reverse engineering. The effect is stronger under heightened competition, when hiring competitors’ employees is restricted, and varies with the product life cycle. For identification, we leverage the Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA). Collectively, our findings highlight reverse engineering as an important but underexplored innovation strategy.

reference: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 808
title: Informal Entrepreneurship: Institutional Drivers and Productivity Consequences
affiliations: Imperial College Business School, Independent, Asian Development Bank - Economic Research and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: Informal Entrepreneurship: Institutional Drivers and Productivity Consequences

publicationDetails.detailsText: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 808

detail.abstract: Using Global Entrepreneurship Monitor and World Bank data, we produce a novel estimation for the prevalence of informal entrepreneurship in 60 countries in the period 2006– 2022. Using a real option framework, we test the effect of business regulation, property rights protection, and the rule of law on formal and informal entrepreneurship prevalence. Finally, we test the influence of a country’s informal entrepreneurship rate on entrepreneurial growth aspirations by individuals. We find that burdensome business regulations increase informal entry relative to formal entry. We also find that stronger property rights and rule of law encourage formal entrepreneurship and discourage informal entrepreneurship. Further, the analysis finds that a high rate of informal entrepreneurship discourages entrepreneurs’ growth aspirations and negatively moderates the relationship between the entrepreneur’s gender and growth aspirations.

title: The United Nations Global Compact and the Sustainable Development Goals
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School

detail.title: The United Nations Global Compact and the Sustainable Development Goals

publicationDetails.detailsText:
In book - Research Handbook of Responsible Management
Publisher - Edward Elgar

detail.abstract: This chapter discusses the relationship between the United Nations (UN) system and the private sector against the background of responsible management practices. The first part discusses the relationship between the UN and private enterprises from a historical perspectives, starting from the 1970s until today. The second part introduces the UN’s flagship initiative for responsible management: the United Nations Global Compact. It reviews the underlying rationale of the initiative as well as its governance framework and perceived legitimacy. The third section discusses the move from the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) to the SDGs, and shows that the SDGs are better aligned with responsible management concerns due to their more explicit emphasis on partnerships and their recognition that social, environmental and economic problems are interconnected. The final section outlines a research agenda that emphasizes areas of scholarly activity related to the UNGC and the SDGs that have so far been neglected.

title: Education as Phenomenon: A Tripartite Model and the Principle of Archesyndesmos
affiliations: Addis Ababa University

detail.title: Education as Phenomenon: A Tripartite Model and the Principle of Archesyndesmos
detail.abstract: This work presents a theoretical framework that reconceptualizes education as an emergent phenomenological event, defined by the tripartite interaction of Being, Transmission, and Receiving. This model is catalyzed by the critical point of contact termed archesyndesmos. The analysis synthesizes extant philosophical critiques of instrumentalist and reified notions of education, leveraging their valid premises to construct a resolution to longstanding ontological ambiguities. The primary scholarly contributions of this paper are, therefore, the introduction of a precise, phenomenological definition of education as the transfer of being to the psyche and the proposition of the foundational concept of archesyndesmos as the transformative mechanism underlying this transfer. Developed through a systematic analysis of foundational principles, this framework seeks to reorient discourse toward the dynamic, relational nature of the educational phenomenon itself.

title: Beyond Skills Mismatch: Incentive-Driven Market Dysfunction in Online Hiring
affiliations: The Job Applicant Perspective

detail.title: Beyond Skills Mismatch: Incentive-Driven Market Dysfunction in Online Hiring

declarations.ethicsApproval: I have used AI to help me organize the paper coherently, as well as edit for syntax and grammar and check reference orders I may have missed but all ideas and concepts here are mine uniquely and I take full responsibility

detail.abstract: The dominant explanation for hiring dysfunction has long been "skills mismatch"-the claim that workers lack the capabilities employers need. While supported by evidence of scarring, polarization, and exclusion, this explanation omits a central structural force: the incentive models of digital hiring platforms. Drawing on fiscal year reports from LinkedIn, Indeed/Recruit Holdings, and related HR technology firms, this paper demonstrates how platform profitability aligns with inefficiency. Revenues rise when vacancies remain unresolved, as each additional posting, resurface, or application generates monetizable circulation. I reexamine major literatures-Harvard Business School's Hidden Workers, longitudinal "Lost Generation" studies, JOLTS hires-to-openings data, ghost job surveys, and polarization analyses-through this lens. Together, they reveal that inefficiency is not merely accidental or supply-side, but systematically rewarded. The analysis reframes job seekers not only as labor supply, but also as unprotected consumers and unpaid revenue drivers. This critique advances a new interpretive frame for labor market research: inefficiency is structural, not personal.

title: Continuous Evaluation of Non-Unionized Staff in Educational Institutions: Issues, Methods and Impact on Performance
affiliations: University of Montreal

detail.title: Continuous Evaluation of Non-Unionized Staff in Educational Institutions: Issues, Methods and Impact on Performance
detail.abstract: Continuous evaluation of non-unionized staff in the implementation of learning is an essential means of improving performance, motivating employees and maintaining the quality of educational service. Non-unionized staff typically include administrative assistants, technicians, academic faculties and other employees who facilitate the establishment of learning but are not well recognized. Continuous evaluation makes it possible to link the individual's objective with institutional missions.

title: The Ascending Trajectory of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Construction and Project Controls
affiliations: , Google LLC and Carnegie Mellon University

detail.title: The Ascending Trajectory of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Construction and Project Controls
detail.abstract: The construction industry, a cornerstone of infrastructure development and economic growth stimulation, has traditionally been one of the more conservative sectors to embrace and adopt digital technologies. This reluctance is now changing into increasingly giving way to an awareness of the disruptive potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in the resolution of its core challenges and hurdles, such as cost overrun, productivity constraints, and shortages of skilled workforce. This paper offers an integrated review of the development and the growth, and evolution of AI/ML applications and solutions within the construction sector, with a particular focus on construction project management and controls. By integrating recent literature, this paper examines the historical trends related to the adoption of AI/ML, evaluates current applications across various project life cycles and phases, and points towards future potential and directions. Additionally, it responds to the specific role of AI/ML in enhancing construction project controls, such as developments and innovations in cost estimation, schedule optimization, risk management, and overall project performance. This analysis provides insightful information to researchers and practitioners seeking to understand and leverage the changing role of AI/ML in constructing a more efficient, safe, sustainable, and cost-reducing construction industry.

title: Income, Democracy, and Growth: Reconciling Evidence and Theory
affiliations: Università di Bologna, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Income, Democracy, and Growth: Reconciling Evidence and Theory
detail.abstract: The relation between income and democracy remains debated, empirically and theoretically. We propose a broader perspective that goes beyond a uni-directional and monocausal interpretation of the income-democracy nexus by focusing on the neglected role of the transition from economic stagnation to sustained growth. We illustrate our argument with an integrated model of long-run growth and democratisation that delivers two general insights. First, rather than higher income levels per se, it is the onset of sustained growth that increases the likelihood of democratisation. Intuitively, the faster accumulation of productive factors, such as human capital, reduces conflicts of interest and hence the elite’s resistance to democracy. Second, the economic consequences of democracy are amplified when democratisation occurs after the transition to growth. We explore the validity of these novel predictions by revisiting influential empirical studies and exploiting variation in the timing of the transition to sustained growth. Our evidence is consistent with the theoretical predictions, shedding new light on the interpretation of earlier mixed findings.

title: Integrating Financial Risk Management and Strategic Investment Decisions in the Context of Digitalization and ESG: A Conceptual Approach to Fiscal Uncertainty in Indonesia
affiliations: Universitas Terbuka

detail.title: Integrating Financial Risk Management and Strategic Investment Decisions in the Context of Digitalization and ESG: A Conceptual Approach to Fiscal Uncertainty in Indonesia
detail.abstract: In the midst of global economic dynamics characterized by massive digitalization, growing demands for sustainability through Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, and rising fiscal uncertainty, firms face significant challenges in making long-term strategic investment decisions. This study synthesizes recent literature (2021-2025) to explore the relationship between financial risk management and strategic investment decisions, while considering the role of digitalization, ESG, and fiscal uncertainty as contextual and moderating variables. The novelty of this study lies in proposing a new conceptual model that integrates three key aspects-financial risk, ESG, and digitalization-within the fiscal uncertainty context of an emerging economy such as Indonesia. This model advances the field of strategic financial management by unifying micro perspectives (finance and technology) with macro perspectives (fiscal policy and sustainability) in a single analytical framework. The findings provide theoretical contributions by extending risk management and investment decision-making literature, and practical implications for corporate policymakers to design more adaptive and resilient investment strategies in response to external uncertainties.

title: African Integration Reimagined: From Continental-Level Aspirations to Regional-Level Realities
affiliations: Desiderio Consultants Ltd. and Université Catholique de Lille

detail.title: African Integration Reimagined: From Continental-Level Aspirations to Regional-Level Realities
detail.abstract: This paper argues that Africa's economic integration must shift from a top-down, aspirational model toward a pragmatic, project-based approach centered on the development of Regional Value Chains (RVCs). While the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) provides an overarching framework for advancing continental integration, persistent challenges-like infrastructural deficits, fragmented production systems, and misaligned regulatory environments-indicate that meaningful progress can only be achieved incrementally. Given Africa's economic and geographic diversity, regionally differentiated strategies are required, with RVCs serving as primary drivers and Regional Economic Communities (RECs) as institutional anchors. By showing how RVC-led integration can align local comparative advantages with broader continental goals, the paper identifies a more viable pathway toward industrialisation that enhances competitiveness, resilience, and technological upgrading.

title: Editorial Authority vs. Reviewer Integrity: The Case for Reviewer Self-Citation Rights
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: Editorial Authority vs. Reviewer Integrity: The Case for Reviewer Self-Citation Rights
detail.abstract: This article critically examines editorial interventions that restrict or modify reviewer self-citations in the peer review process, using a recent case at Physica Scripta as a focal point. It argues that reviewers possess unique expertise regarding their own works and are often best positioned to provide precise, contextually relevant recommendations-including citations to their research. The removal or modification of such recommendations by editors, without reviewer consent, undermines the integrity of the peer review system, diminishes reviewer autonomy, and may impede the correction of scientific errors. Furthermore, the article highlights the contradiction between commercial self-promotion in publishing and the penalization of scholarly self-citation, framing these restrictions as manifestations of academic gamification that privilege institutional interests over genuine scientific progress. The work calls for transparent, evidencebased policies that respect reviewer rights and uphold the ethical standards of scholarly communication.

title: Optimal Transit Prices in the Presence of High Fare Evasion and Weak Enforcement *
affiliations: University of Chile - Department of Economics and University of Chile

detail.title: Optimal Transit Prices in the Presence of High Fare Evasion and Weak Enforcement *
detail.abstract: We analyze the impact of fare evasion on the optimal transit fare under weak enforcement, motivated by the case of Santiago, Chile. We derive analytical expressions for the optimal fares for two scenarios: when the central planner does not consider evader trips in the determination of the system's supply and quality variables and when the central planner designs the operational plan according to total demand, including fare dodgers. The main result is that fare evasion tends to lower the optimal fare compared to a benchmark without evasion, especially in the scenario where the planner considers all users when determining the supply variables. Parameterizing the model for Santiago indicates that the current fare should increase in the first scenario but should decrease under the second scenario. The derived model could be applied to other cities suffering from rising fare non-payment rates and weak enforcement capabilities.

title: Algorithmic Hiring and Emirati Labour: Balancing Efficiency, Equity, and Cultural Context
affiliations: International Islamic University Islamabad

detail.title: Algorithmic Hiring and Emirati Labour: Balancing Efficiency, Equity, and Cultural Context
detail.abstract: This research article critically investigates the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment systems within the United Arab Emirates (UAE), focusing on its intersection with Emiratisation policies, labor governance, and emerging data protection frameworks. While AIbased hiring tools are frequently promoted for efficiency, scalability, and policy alignment, this study highlights their potential to reproduce structural inequities, obscure accountability, and reinforce global hierarchies of privilege. Drawing upon policy documents, recent UAE government initiatives, and global literature on algorithmic bias (O'Neil, 2016; Noble, 2018), the paper demonstrates how AI-enabled recruitment can simultaneously advance state objectives and entrench systemic exclusions. The analysis further explores the UAE's unique sociocultural and demographic context, where Emiratisation goals, expatriate dominance, and data governance converge. Ultimately, the paper argues for a governance-first approach that prioritizes transparency, fairness, and cultural sensitivity in AI-driven HR systems. Practical policy recommendations are offered for regulators, employers, and vendors to ensure that AI fosters inclusion, equity, and sustainable labor market development in the UAE.

title: From the Particular to the Generic: Fostering A More Socioeconomically Diverse Professoriate
affiliations: University of Illinois Springfield

detail.title: From the Particular to the Generic: Fostering A More Socioeconomically Diverse Professoriate

keywords: Students for Fair Admissions vs Harvard

detail.abstract:
In an introductory editorial to a 2023 symposium issue of Public Administration Review, Stivers et al. recount the contents of several publications about social justice and social equity. She and her colleagues end their editorial by proposing that public administration scholars develop a normative plan leading to greater social equity and social justice for members of the disadvantaged groups they, Stivers and her coauthors, identify in their editorial.

Responding to this call for reform, the present project addresses the problem of structural nepotism (inherited wealth based on Bourdieu’s three identified forms), a notable concern that Stivers and her colleagues and the nine symposium contributors fail to consider in full despite what the former say about how “canonize[d]” values limit the range of social equity and social justice questions public administration scholars confront. Employing comments and citations Stivers et al. offer throughout their editorial, the second part of this discussion offers a plan for resolving many of the harmful effects of structural nepotism on both the theory and practice of social equity and social justice in one academic discipline. The reform suggested herein is generic and thus readily adaptable to all fields of study.

title: Unicorn Investing: Measuring and Predicting the Rise of Billion-Dollar Startups
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: Unicorn Investing: Measuring and Predicting the Rise of Billion-Dollar Startups
detail.abstract: This paper examines the emergence of unicorns, privately held startups valued at over $1 billion, as a distinct investment phenomenon. We introduce a Unicorn Index, a systematic framework to score and predict unicorn potential based on market size, scalability, innovation, team quality, and funding network. Using case studies of Stripe, NVIDIA, and Coinbase, we illustrate how early signals can anticipate unicorn outcomes. We argue that unicorn investing combines traditional venture capital principles with rare, stochastic outcomes, blending skill with luck. The paper concludes with implications for investors, policymakers, and educators.

title: Music as an Asset Class
affiliations: Cornell Financial Engineering Manhattan, Cornell University - Department of Computer Science, Cornell University and Cornell University

detail.title: Music as an Asset Class
detail.abstract: In the streaming era, music revenues distributed to rights holders have become more transparent. However, it is not yet clear how to quantify the risk and return characteristics of music royalty assets, as is done with equities. In this paper, we fit three discounted cashflow models to transactions on the Royalty Exchange platform. We use our best model to backtest the one year and five year performance of music royalty assets, after transaction costs. We find that Life of Rights (LOR) music assets had risk and return characteristics comparable to stocks in the S&P500, when held over 5 years. Since the performance of stocks and music assets are likely to be uncorrelated, this result may help investors assess this asset class within the context of a more traditional stock and bond portfolio.

title: Confronting the Fear: Understanding and Overcoming Retaliation in Academic Criticism
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: Confronting the Fear: Understanding and Overcoming Retaliation in Academic Criticism
detail.abstract: This paper examines the pervasive fear of retaliation that discourages critical discourse in academic publishing, using recent rejection patterns as empirical evidence. Through analysis of editorial gatekeeping mechanisms and systematic suppression tactics, we demonstrate how the academic publishing system has evolved sophisticated methods to silence criticism while maintaining an appearance of objective scholarly standards. The study reveals that fear of retaliation is not merely psychological but reflects documented patterns of editorial bias, procedural manipulation, and institutional protection mechanisms. By examining specific cases of rejection based on artificial criteria such as self-citation thresholds, submission frequency limits, and scope manipulation, we show how publishers systematically exclude critical voices while avoiding direct engagement with substantive arguments. The paper argues that confronting criticism constructively requires institutional reforms that protect dissenting voices, establish transparent editorial practices, and prioritize intellectual merit over conformity to established paradigms.

title: From Free to Fee: How Allowance Allocation Affects ETS Performance
affiliations: European University Institute, European University Institute - Economics Department (ECO) and European University Institute - Economics Department (ECO)

detail.title: From Free to Fee: How Allowance Allocation Affects ETS Performance
detail.abstract: This study provides causal firm-level estimates of the effect of a reduction in free emission allowances in emission trading systems on emissions and economic performance. We study an EU ETS reform that withdrew the right of some manufacturing firms to receive most emission allowances for free, exploiting this change in a differencein-differences setting. We find that paying for allowances decreased emissions by more than 11 percent overall, relative to firms that retained free allowances. This reduction was accompanied by a significant decrease in economic performance, including revenue, employment, and assets of a similar magnitude. Using a multi-product model, we show that our results can be rationalized through an extensive margin adjustment of firms.

title: GITT: Essentials, Uses, and Usage
affiliations: Phenikaa University, Phenikaa University, Phenikaa University and Phenikaa University

detail.title: GITT: Essentials, Uses, and Usage
detail.abstract: This material represents an ongoing effort to share our thesis and understanding with other publishing authors working on their research studies in the disciplines of the humanities and social sciences. The document discusses our homegrown Granular Interaction Thinking and Information Theory hypothesis (abbreviated as GITT) in a practical way. It is not long and is structured fairly simply. In the first part, some background information is provided so that readers can know where the idea came from. The next one presents essentials that enable someone new to it can grasp its nitty-gritty. The third part deals with basic mathematical concepts that can enable us to develop applications of GITT more aptly during the research process. The fourth part is dedicated to circumstances or examples where GITT applications show their usefulness. This is also where we can discuss what could have been done better, and under what conditions. This part certainly borrows pieces of real-world publications, all of which will be properly referenced for the sake of integrity and further examination. The last one presents worthwhile remarks and caveats, which will be of use to those who want to try out the GITT framework. When and where appropriate, we will consider adding new content or even new parts to make the material more useful to readers. Thus, the document can be continually expanding alongside the real-world applications of GITT.

title: Promoting Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB): Unintended Gender Disparities in the Participation and Evaluation of Different Types of OCB
affiliations: Tulane University - A.B. Freeman School of Business, University of Texas at Arlington - Department of Accounting, Vienna University of Economics and Business - Institute for Markets and Strategy and Goizueta Business School

detail.title: Promoting Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB): Unintended Gender Disparities in the Participation and Evaluation of Different Types of OCB

contentType.other: Accepted for publication in the January 2026 issue of The Accounting Review

detail.abstract: Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB), employees voluntarily going "above and beyond" their defined job responsibilities, is important for organizational success. We examine unintended consequences of using a management control system to promote and reward OCBs. Specifically, because OCB transcends pre-established core job performance criteria, valuation of OCB necessarily relies on subjective judgments, allowing for gender stereotypes to manifest. Using proprietary data from a financial services firm, we examine two types of OCBs, agentic OCB and communal OCB. Consistent with gender stereotypes, women are less likely to participate in agentic OCB and more likely to participate in communal OCB. Consistent with “shifting standards” theory, we find that men obtain a significant evaluation premium for communal OCB, while women obtain a marginal evaluation premium for agentic OCB. Our findings build upon research showing career benefits of OCB, on average, to show gender differences in the value organizations place on different types of OCB.

title: Green Growth: The Role of Corporate Sustainability in Achieving India’s Net Zero 2070 Goals

detail.title: Green Growth: The Role of Corporate Sustainability in Achieving India’s Net Zero 2070 Goals

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The research was conducted independently, and all interpretations, findings, and conclusions are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve any experiments on humans or animals, nor did it require the collection of personal or sensitive data. All materials used are secondary sources, publicly available reports, and academic publications. As such, no formal ethics approval was required for the preparation of this paper.

detail.abstract: India's pledge to achieve Net Zero emissions by 2070, announced at the COP26 Summit, represents one of the most ambitious climate commitments globally. While national policies set the framework, it is Indian corporates that will determine the pace and feasibility of this transition. Corporates contribute a significant share of greenhouse gas emissions but also possess the resources, technologies, and influence to drive sustainable growth. This paper examines the evolving role of corporate sustainability in aligning business strategies with India's Net Zero target. It highlights the shift from traditional Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks, emphasizing how sustainability is no longer a peripheral activity but a central business strategy. Through case studies of leading Indian companies such as Tata Group, Reliance Industries, Infosys, Mahindra, and ITC, the paper demonstrates how investments in renewable energy, green hydrogen, circular economy practices, and digital transformation are reshaping the corporate landscape. However, challenges such as inconsistent regulation, high capital costs, skills shortages, and greenwashing continue to obstruct progress. The paper argues that achieving Net Zero 2070 will require corporates to move beyond symbolic initiatives and embed sustainability into their core business models. Policy support, green finance, innovation, and public-private collaboration will be critical enablers of this shift. Ultimately, the study concludes that corporate sustainability is not only essential for meeting India's Net Zero goals but also represents a pathway to long-term competitiveness, investor trust, and green growth.

title: Should Arbitrators be Immune from Liability?

detail.title: Should Arbitrators be Immune from Liability?
detail.abstract: In resolving disputes, arbitrators perform the role of adjudication. Their role is resembled to and often referred to as arbitrators acting in 'quasi-judicial capacity' such that arbitrators, in many important jurisdictions, are granted immunity akin to those afforded to judges known as 'judicial immunity'. However, professionals working in different disciplines are not granted any such immunity. If that is the case with all other professionals, why should arbitrators be granted immunity? On the contrary, arbitrators perform an important function of adjudicating which relieves the national and international court systems from the influx of thousands of disputes every year while rendering awards in an efficient and effective manner suitable for business needs as opposed to lengthy litigation process. Given the important functions arbitrators perform that can be referred to as quasi-judicial function, it justifies their enjoying immunity in this capacity otherwise arbitrators would not feel safe to act as such. The article develops on these two dimensions as outlined above and sheds light on the background to judicial and arbitral immunity, the cases for and against the notion of arbitral immunity, the different approaches taken by various jurisdictions on this subject matter from a comparative and a critical perspective.

title: From Party Tools to Symbolic Engines: Rethinking Think Tanks in Latin America and Beyond
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Party Tools to Symbolic Engines: Rethinking Think Tanks in Latin America and Beyond

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial or personal interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, patients, or sensitive personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It is conducted as part of the author’s independent research.

detail.abstract:
This paper reexamines the strategic role of think tanks in Latin America, moving beyond their conventional portrayal as party instruments. Building on the empirical framework of Barreda and Ruiz Rodríguez (2022), who developed a “strategic relevance index” to measure party–think tank linkages across eight countries, the analysis acknowledges the value of comparative data while also addressing the study’s limitations. Quantitative indicators, though useful, risk overlooking the symbolic, cultural, and discursive dimensions that shape legitimacy and political imagination.

By engaging with Latin American intellectual traditions—such as O’Donnell’s reflections on fragile democracies, Cardoso and Faletto’s theory of dependency, and Castañeda’s work on ideological realignments—the paper emphasizes the importance of ideas, narratives, and symbols in understanding democratic development. Think tanks, it argues, should not be understood as mere satellites of political parties but as laboratories of political imagination with the capacity to generate frameworks of democracy, legitimacy, and justice.

The findings underscore the need to strengthen intellectual independence, foster regional and global networks, and situate Latin American experiences within the wider debates of the Global South.

title: 2025 Southeast Asia Eleven Nations Influence Index Report
affiliations: Dhurakij Pundit University

detail.title: 2025 Southeast Asia Eleven Nations Influence Index Report
detail.abstract: This study aims to construct a fully data-driven and reproducible Southeast Asia Influence Index (SAII v3) to overcome biases from expert scoring and subjective weighting, while mapping the hierarchical power structure across the eleven ASEAN nations. Methodologically, we aggregate authoritative open-source indicators across four dimensions-economic, military, diplomatic, and socio-technological-applying a three-tiered standardization chain ("quantile-Box-Cox-min-max") to reduce outliers and skewness. Weights are obtained through an equal-weight integration of three methods: Entropy Weighting Method (EWM), CRITIC, and PCA. Robustness testing is conducted using Kendall's Tau, ±20% weight perturbation and 10,000 bootstrap iterations to ensure robustness. Additionally, ±10% dimensional sensitivity analysis and V2-V3 bump chart comparisons were conducted. Results indicate the integrated weights are approximately: Economy 35%-40%, Military 20%-25%, Diplomacy ≈20%, Socio-Technology ≈15%. The overall landscape presents a "one strong, two medium, three stable, and multiple weak" pattern, with Indonesia, Singapore, and Malaysia leading, while Thailand, the Philippines, and Vietnam form a mid-tier competitive band. V2 and V3 rankings showed high consistency (Kendall's Tau=0.818), though minor mid-tier reordering occurred (Thailand and Philippines rose, Vietnam fell), indicating V3's greater sensitivity to structural equilibrium. ASEAN-11 average sensitivity further highlighted military and socio-technological dimensions as having the greatest marginal effects (±0.002). In conclusion, SAII v3 achieves algorithmic weighting and auditable reproducibility methodologically, empirically reveals multidimensional drivers of influence in Southeast Asia, and provides actionable quantitative evidence for resource allocation and policy prioritization by regional nations and external partners.

title: A Two-Period Model of Reference Pricing with Product Design
affiliations: Universitat de València and University of Valencia

detail.title: A Two-Period Model of Reference Pricing with Product Design
detail.abstract: We examine the linkages between endogenous product design and optimal pricing under consumer reference price effects. With a monopolist firm, our analysis shows that product design affects the optimal price markdown that arises from intertemporal reference effects. The monopolist uses markdown pricing to transform sales from the reference period into sales in the discount period. Then, more customized designs lead to greater price markdowns. A similar pattern emerges with product market competition, but market rivalry limits the extent to which markdowns can be used for intertemporal transformation of sales. Here, product design can lead to price-increasing competition if firms have strong incentives to target their niche consumers with more customized designs when the degree of competition increases, and this sets the stage for markdown-increasing competition in which prices in different periods increase with new firm entry, but the reference price increases relatively more.

title: Customer Satisfaction: Past Research, Strategic Outcomes, and Future Directions
affiliations: Rice University,  and University of Texas at San Antonio

detail.title: Customer Satisfaction: Past Research, Strategic Outcomes, and Future Directions
detail.abstract: Customer satisfaction (CSAT) has long been recognized as a central construct in marketing theory and practice, yet its role as a strategic resource is often underappreciated. This article synthesizes the conceptual foundations, measurement approaches, empirical findings, and managerial applications of customer satisfaction research. We define CSAT as a post-consumption evaluative judgment of whether customers receive the promised value, and we distinguish it from related constructs such as service quality, engagement, loyalty, experience, and value. Drawing on multiple scales and a comparative study across consumer demographics, we demonstrate that widely used CSAT measures exhibit strong convergent validity. We review the historical evolution of CSAT research, highlighting its progression from expectancy-disconfirmation models to integrated frameworks linking customer perceptions, loyalty intentions, and firm performance. Using a large-scale dataset of over 285 million ratings across 1,126 brands, we replicate and extend prior meta-analytic evidence by showing that CSAT is robustly associated with customer mindset metrics, accounting outcomes, and stock market performance. Importantly, we quantify the economic value of marginal changes in CSAT for representative firms. We conclude by developing micro and macro-level conceptual frameworks and outlining a forward-looking research agenda to revitalize marketing's leadership in customer satisfaction scholarship and practice.

title: The Effect of Strategic Marketing on Creating Competitive Advantages of the Dairy Industry in Kosovo
affiliations: ,  and AAB College

detail.title: The Effect of Strategic Marketing on Creating Competitive Advantages of the Dairy Industry in Kosovo
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of marketing strategies on creating competitive advantage through strategies such as customized products strategy, pricing strategy, distribution strategy, promotion strategy, and innovation orientation strategy. The study was carried out on the basis of primary data, where part of the quantitative research were 15 categorized dairies, with low capacity (300-3,000 liters per day), with medium capacity (5,000-100,000 liters per day), and with high capacity (over 100,000 liters per day). From these dairies, 150 workers in leadership positions were surveyed, from which the marketing strategy with the greatest impact on creating competitive advantages was identified. Questionnaires were physically distributed and data were processed through Statistical Package for Social Sciences, version 26. Based on the multiple regression analysis, it was found that there is a statistically significant correlation that marketing strategies affect the creation of competitive advantage based on the value of R-square = 0.787, where customized products strategy, price strategy, and distribution strategy were found as important strategies. While innovation strategy and promotion strategy left the model due to the increased value of significance p > 0.05. Through this study, the dairy industry receives feedback on the type of strategy that should be used to create a competitive advantage, more so in the specific case where imports are very high and competition is very fierce.

title: Engagement vs. Commitment: The Economic Trade-Offs of Polarizing News Content
affiliations: HEC Paris and HEC Paris (Groupe HEC), Students

detail.title: Engagement vs. Commitment: The Economic Trade-Offs of Polarizing News Content
detail.abstract: We study how polarizing content shapes two economic outcomes on a major European news website: engagement (time on site) and commitment (paid subscriptions). Using advances in natural language processing, we construct deep-learning and large-language-model-based textual measures of polarization tailored to a multiparty system. We combine comprehensive supply and demand data-the full publisher-wide article inventory with user-level clicks and subscription outcomes-to track how consumers interact with polarizing articles. To identify causal effects, we use two theoretically distinct instruments: (i) a Bartik-style design that interacts users' stable topic preferences with weekly shifts in the supply of polarizing content; and (ii) an election shock that raises political salience for a subset of readers. We document a "polarization trap": exogenous increases in exposure to polarizing content raise engagement (time on site) but reduce the probability of subscribing. The negative subscription effect is driven more by the affective than the ideological dimension of polarization and is strongest during high-salience political periods. These results imply a strategic trade-off for publishers: content that maximizes short-run attention can undermine the formation of a loyal, paying subscriber base.

title: Impact of Customer Feedback on Business Performance: A Study on JK Tyre, Bengaluru
affiliations: BNM Institute of Technology

detail.title: Impact of Customer Feedback on Business Performance: A Study on JK Tyre, Bengaluru

All participants were informed about the purpose of the research, and their consent was obtained prior to data collection. Anonymity and confidentiality of responses were assured. detail.abstract: Customer feedback serves as a critical input for organizations aiming to sustain growth in competitive markets. This study explores the influence of customer feedback on business performance, with specific reference to JK Tyre in Bengaluru. Primary data was gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to customers and dealers, focusing on satisfaction, interaction patterns, and service perceptions. The findings indicate that although many respondents maintain long-term associations with JK Tyre, certain gaps persist in service responsiveness and complaint management. The research highlights the need for structured feedback systems to enhance loyalty, operational efficiency, and market competitiveness.

title: Watch with Me: Danmaku Comments and Viewer Endorsements on Video-Sharing Platforms
affiliations: University of Delaware - Alfred Lerner College of Business and Economics , Indiana University Bloomington - Kelley School of Business and

detail.title: Watch with Me: Danmaku Comments and Viewer Endorsements on Video-Sharing Platforms
detail.abstract: Danmaku is a video comment function that displays user-generated comments as flying text synchronized with video playback. Despite its widespread use and popularity, research on its impact remains underexplored. This study theorizes and tests how two content features of Danmaku-information intensity and emotion density-affect video endorsements (likes and virtual rewards) on a large video-sharing platform. Leveraging panel data from 15,211 videos by 2,746 creators over seven days, we analyze the effects of Danmaku content features on endorsements, controlling for video and day fixed effects and daily views. We find that (1) both information intensity and emotion density positively influence likes and rewards; (2) they act as substitutes to influence rewards but not likes; (3) their effects vary by video type-information intensity has a stronger impact for information-oriented videos, whereas emotion density is more influential for entertainment-oriented videos. These findings enhance our understanding of how and why a highly dynamic and interactive viewing experience, such as Danmaku, influences video endorsements and provide practical implications for improving engagement on videosharing platforms.

title: The Perilous Path of Economic Nationalism: A Call for Reason in a Globalized World
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Perilous Path of Economic Nationalism: A Call for Reason in a Globalized World

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with organizations that could have influenced this study. This research was conducted independently without institutional affiliation or external funding that could create conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved analysis of publicly available documents, expert commentary, and published data sources. No human subjects research was conducted, therefore formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the resurgence of economic nationalism and protectionist trade policies through analysis of expert commentary from the 2025 Antalya Diplomacy Forum. Drawing on insights from Professor Jeffrey Sachs and international finance ministers, the analysis critiques recent tariff policies that have contributed to significant market volatility, including over $6.6 trillion in U.S. market losses in April 2025. The paper demonstrates how bilateral trade deficit targeting reflects fundamental misunderstandings of market economics while undermining multilateral institutions. Against the backdrop of accelerating climate change (0.36°C per decade warming rate) and record global debt levels (328% of GDP), the analysis argues that economic nationalism represents a dangerous retreat from the international cooperation required to address systemic global challenges. The paper concludes that evidence-based policy approaches emphasizing comparative advantage and multilateral coordination offer superior alternatives to protectionist responses to technological disruption and global economic shifts.

title: Green Inside, Silent Outside? The Sustainability Branding Dilemma in Indian Pharma
affiliations: S.B.Patil Institute of Management and S.B.Patil Institute of Management

detail.title: Green Inside, Silent Outside? The Sustainability Branding Dilemma in Indian Pharma

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests. This case study was developed for academic and educational purposes only, and no personal or financial relationship has influenced its preparation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work is a teaching case study based on secondary data and does not involve human participants or patients. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: India's pharmaceutical industry is facing growing pressure to adopt sustainable practices, driven by regulations such as the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework, stricter norms from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), and SEBI's ESG disclosure requirements, alongside global commitments like the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). While these rules ensure compliance, they also create opportunities for companies to use sustainability as a differentiator. This case focuses on BioPharm MedTech, a mid-sized Indian company that has introduced initiatives such as biodegradable packaging, carbon footprint audits, renewable energy use, and sustainable supply chain practices. Despite these efforts, the company is hesitant to highlight its actions externally, fearing accusations of greenwashing in a trust-sensitive sector. The case presents a strategic dilemma: should BioPharm remain "silent green," quietly compliant, or move toward "loud green" branding by incorporating sustainability into its marketing through the emerging concept of the "Green P"? The discussion invites students to weigh regulatory demands, stakeholder expectations, and reputational risks to decide whether sustainability should remain an internal practice or be leveraged as a driver of brand equity and differentiation. Beyond the company-specific decision, the case also illustrates broader challenges faced by Indian firms in highly regulated, trust-sensitive sectors. It is designed to enhance students' ability to connect regulatory frameworks with branding strategy, critically assess the risks of greenwashing, and apply the 7Ps marketing framework, consisting of the six traditional Ps (Product, Price, Place, Promotion, People, and Process) along with the Green P representing sustainability as the seventh in a practical context.

title: Advancing Marketing Video Analysis with Multimodal LLMs and Context-Aware GraphRAG
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison, University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Marketing and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Advancing Marketing Video Analysis with Multimodal LLMs and Context-Aware GraphRAG
detail.abstract: Video data is increasingly accessible across marketing contexts; however, its potential remains largely untapped due to the complexity of analyzing multimodal content and deriving interpretable, nuanced insights. This paper proposes a novel framework that combines  Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with contextual knowledge sources, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and knowledge graph-based GraphRAG. While RAG allows us to enhance standard MLLMs with domain-specific information, improving both accuracy and interpretability, it still falls short in incorporating human feedback from contextually labeled video data. GraphRAG addresses this limitation by effectively modeling the relationships among entities within the video content. We demonstrate the utility of our framework by applying it to the analysis of influencer authenticity, a key determinant in influencer marketing. By integrating domain knowledge through RAG and aligning model outputs with human-coded authenticity assessments via GraphRAG, our approach achieves around 19% reduction in prediction error, surpassing prior transformer-based video classification methods and multi-modal LLMs that do not incorporate context. Moreover, it delivers context-specific, actionable insights for different influencer and audience segments, addressing elements such as pitch modulation, background music, body language, and product choice.

title: Investigating the Impact of Social Media Advertising on Customer Purchase Intention: A Quantitative Study
affiliations: Institute of Technology & Management (ITM), Jiwaji University and ITM University Gwalior

detail.title: Investigating the Impact of Social Media Advertising on Customer Purchase Intention: A Quantitative Study
detail.abstract: This quantitative study explores the influence of social media advertising on customer purchase intention by analyzing various advertising features and metrics. With the proliferation of social media platforms, businesses are increasingly investing in advertising to engage with their target audience. However, understanding the effectiveness of these advertising efforts in driving consumer behavior remains essential yet challenging. This research aims to bridge this gap by conducting a quantitative analysis of social media advertising strategies and their impact on customer purchase intention. The study utilizes a structured survey questionnaire administered to a sample of social media users, focusing on their perceptions and behaviors in response to different types of social media advertising. Key variables examined include ad content relevance, targeting options, interactivity, and engagement metrics. Statistical analysis techniques, such as regression analysis, will be employed to identify significant relationships between these variables and customer purchase intention. Expected findings include insights into which advertising features have the most significant influence on customer purchase intention and how engagement metrics correlate with advertising effectiveness. The results of this study can provide valuable guidance for businesses seeking to optimize their social media advertising strategies and maximize their return on investment in digital marketing efforts.

title: Leveraging NLP and Sentiment Analysis for ML-Based Fake News Detection with Big Data
affiliations: Wright State University, University of Illinois at Springfield, University of Central Missouri, University of Bridgeport, University of Illinois at Springfield and Fairleigh Dickinson University

detail.title: Leveraging NLP and Sentiment Analysis for ML-Based Fake News Detection with Big Data
detail.abstract: As a critical cybersecurity tool, Natural Language Processing (NLP) provides an automated the quick dissemination of misleading information online, necessitating the use of a fake news detecting system. The suggested fake news detection system incorporates sentiment analysis with a number of machine learning (ML) and deep learning models, such as Random Forest (RF) and Logistic Regression (LR) algorithms, Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Naive Bayes (NB), in addition to a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network solution. The study involved extensive data preprocessing, TF-IDF, and Bag-of-Words feature extraction. The model was then evaluated using binary cross-entropy loss, accuracy and precision, recall, and F1-score assessments. Through efficient sequential and contextual text processing, the LSTM model outperformed other models in the Kaggle fake news dataset, which had over 26,000 items. In experimental evaluation, LSTM outperformed the convolutional neural network (CNN) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models, achieving 95.1% accuracy, 94.4% precision, 95.3% recall, and 94.2% F1-score. LSTM deep learning (DL) algorithms demonstrate exceptional reliability in identifying deceptive content because they perform better than traditional machine learning methods, thus offering great potential as a basic cybersecurity tool to stop misinformation spread.

title: The Theory of Profit Discrimination: A Formal Model

detail.title: The Theory of Profit Discrimination: A Formal Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: \section*{Declaration of Interest Statement} The author declares that there is no known personal or financial conflict of interest that could have appeared to influence the study reported in this article.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or animals.

detail.abstract: This article proposes a formal model to understand discrimination as a profit-oriented economic activity. In contrast to essentialist conceptions, we assume that any individual may engage in discriminatory behavior if there is a prospect of gains. The framework emphasizes: (i) the cumulative nature of initial advantage; and (ii) the optimal choice between discriminating and responding. We derive best-response curves, illustrate the equilibrium (d * , r *), and compare three policy scenarios (baseline, support to the responding agent, and sanction to the discriminator). The conclusion is placed immediately after the figures to facilitate reading.

title: Big Tech in the Courtroom: An Index of Federal Antitrust Filings
